summary: Your plan compares dissolving time at different water temperatures, but the amounts, temperatures, and the way you decide the sugar has dissolved are not specified yet. Clarify these with your TA so the comparison is fair and repeatable.
missingInformation: The volume of water in each cup.
The mass of sugar added to each cup.
The two (or more) water temperatures and how they will be measured.
Whether and how the mixture is stirred.
How you will decide that the sugar has fully dissolved.

findings.title: Comparison conditions are unspecified
findings.explanation: If the cups differ in water volume, sugar mass, or stirring as well as temperature, you cannot tell whether temperature caused any difference in dissolving time.
findings.nextStep: Ask your TA which variables should be held constant and record them before starting.

findings.title: End point of dissolving is subjective
findings.explanation: "When the sugar disappears" can be judged differently by different people or under different lighting, which adds timing error.
findings.nextStep: Agree on a clear end point and consider repeating each condition to see how much the times vary.

findings.title: Single trials limit interpretation
findings.explanation: One trial per temperature cannot show whether a difference is larger than normal run-to-run variation.
findings.nextStep: Ask your TA how many repeats are expected for this exercise.

questionsForTA: What water temperatures should I compare, and how should I measure them?
How much water and sugar should each cup contain?
Should the cups be stirred, and if so, how?
Are there handling rules for hot water at my bench?
